head: 065c4cf32df664d598cde94945409cb937f9bc31
classification_reasons: Blast radius is not small even though the spec is now tight: the plan still touches a brand-new module (plugin/lessons/index.py), a new gate check function registered in CHECKS_BY_PHASE['e'], two command files, two templates, OPERATING_MODEL.md and a two-manifest version bump, and the plan's own Risk 2 still names the gate check as the riskiest step because a wrong guard would silently stop enforcing the lesson/eval invariant for every future incident.

Code is not already covered by existing tests: plugin/lessons/index.py and the new lesson_and_eval check are new, with no prior coverage; the plan schedules new tests (test_lessons.py, new test_gate.py cases, test_commands_and_skills.py extensions) rather than relying on anything existing.

The spec is tighter than last round (both open flagged concerns the owner's review targeted are now closed with an explicit decision, including the reopened-and-reclosed Windows-newline concern), but tight-spec is only one of the three routine conditions and the other two (small blast radius, existing test coverage) still fail.
attempted: Intent: re-checked the fixed spec.md/plan.md against intent.md's Proposed outcome field-by-field; no scope drift introduced by the fix round, and the two carried-forward open questions (sharing across projects, eval-case frontmatter) are still correctly left to their named owners.

Spec and plan: went through all 20 numbered requests in evidence/fix-requests.json one by one against the current spec.md/plan.md text. All 20 are applied faithfully, including the two trickiest ones: (a) the gate check is now a separate lesson_and_eval function guarded by `ctx.status.entry_route == "incident" and ctx.phase == "e"` and registered in CHECKS_BY_PHASE['e'] only, with the gate (f) regression test named as the guard (request 2/3); (b) concern 3 (Windows newline stability) is explicitly reopened and reclosed with the corrected mechanism (write_text(newline='\n') + universal-newline read + as_posix links), not the wrong yamlish.dump_file claim (request 7). Found one residual, minor inconsistency the fix round did not fully propagate: spec.md's Acceptance bullet still enumerates 6 fail-case tests for the new gate check (missing lesson, missing eval case, failing index.py check, dangling supersedes, supersedes-not-retired, out-of-enum status), while plan.md consistently lists 7 in three places (Order of work step 2, the test_gate.py file item, and Proof), adding 'missing a required frontmatter field' as its own case. This is the same class of count mismatch the owner's request 10 flagged last round, now recurring in smaller form between the two documents; it does not block the build because plan.md (the document an implementer actually follows for test scope, per its own closing line) is complete and self-consistent at 7, so I did not treat it as blocking, but it is worth a one-line tidy-up of spec.md's Acceptance bullet in the next pass.

Proof: no code exists yet at this phase (b is design-only); evidence/hook-log.jsonl shows only Edit access to spec.md and plan.md across both sessions (test_file_lock, protected_paths, secrets_check, format_on_edit all 'allow', no guardrail or source-file touches), consistent with a design-phase fix round; evidence/gate-b.json and claude-b.json are the prior round's records (different HEAD, 543f3b9) and were read only for context, never cited as evidence for or against this diff.

Blast radius: cross-checked every corrected file:line citation from the fix request against the actual code: plugin/gate/checks.py's existing entry_route=="incident" branch at lines 205-211 (confirmed it sits inside the artifact-loop check for intent.md, which check_artifacts runs at every phase a-f — confirming the owner's critique that the original design would have mis-fired at gate (f)); CHECKS_BY_PHASE['e'] (1646-1660) and ['f'] (1665+) confirmed phase (f) carries no lesson/eval check today and is a disjoint tuple from (e), so the new check, added only to (e)'s tuple, cannot affect (f); plugin/detect/finding.py lines 54/58/61/62/64 (metric/at/tier/rule) and 146-162 (read_any's scan-record mapping, metric/rule/tier exactly as cited); plugin/detect/routes.py's Resolved (56) and Proposal (81) classes; plugin/state/status.py's id/title/entry_route/build_pr at 36/38/44/89 (and confirmed runbook_authorized_by was correctly dropped from the field-sources list once runbook sourcing was corrected); tests/test_gate.py's _ctx helper at 364 and the maintain_project/test_gate_f_... fixture at 2306-2338/2341-2354 (confirmed exact, replacing the prior round's wrong 2346-2364 citation). Every corrected citation checked out against the real file.

Policies: confirmed data-conventions rules 1 and 3 are still correctly applied to the 'no risk_list item applies' and 'no personal data' claims; confirmed template/sdlc.yaml and docs/OPERATING_MODEL.md are correctly treated as ordinary plugin content (not this repo's own guardrails) per CLAUDE.md's guardrail list, and the diff itself touches neither this repo's own sdlc.yaml/CLAUDE.md/REVIEW.md/.claude/** nor any workflow template.

The tests: plan.md's fail-case list for the new gate check (now seven, each tied to one line of rendered "what I need from you" text) and test_lessons.py's list (ordering, Retired/Unsorted order, README.md/index.md exclusion, malformed frontmatter, zero lessons, (stale) with --today, CRLF check, class normalisation, a body line that looks like YAML to prove the frontmatter split stops at the second '---') each target a specific way the implementation could be wrong rather than one aggregate assertion; this is a design-phase fix round touching no test file, so the pre-existing-test-weakening rule does not apply.
